title: 📰 AI news · November 5

items.title: DreamHost: two months of a breached file manager
items.text: From August to October 23, an outsider collected FTP logins and passwords from people who used DreamHost's web file manager. If your site or bot lives on a host, that login opens every project file, and keys often sit next to the code. Check your site files for unexpected changes and change any password you reuse.

items.title: Google Calendar invites steal logins along with codes
items.text: Since August, invites arrive from a familiar organization and lead to a Google sign-in page relayed through the scammers' server. SMS and app codes are passed along, so two-step protection does not stop it. If you sign in to Google with work or project accounts, check which devices and sessions are open right now.

items.title: APT29 infected iPhones and Androids through websites
items.text: The group swapped the Plerdy analytics script that thousands of sites loaded. On iPhone it took WhatsApp and Telegram databases, keychain passwords and photos; on Android, cookies, logins and Wi-Fi passwords. If you open unfamiliar sites on your phone, make sure the system and browser are up to date.

items.title: A Trojan was planted in the NIKKE launcher
items.text: The game launcher's scripts were tampered with, and since September 27 it installed a remote-access program that stole account and wallet data. The game has over 45 million downloads. If you work on a project on that computer, check which passwords and keys are stored on it. Free guide "Protect your computer, code and access" — send the word "protect" to the bot.

items.title: A Codex kit puts ads into the agent's answers
items.text: Check Point found a kit called Haiou. It edits OpenAI Codex settings files, and ads for a third-party AI gateway appear in the agent's replies. If your agent reads instructions from settings files, check who changed them and when.

items.title: ChatGPT now makes animated GIFs
items.text: The Images 2.6 model creates a GIF from text or a photo. You can edit speed and individual frames, and the character stays recognizable. It is rolling out to all ChatGPT and Codex users.

items.title: GPT-6 Astra rewrites other AI models' weights
items.text: MIT researchers showed the model can change another network's weights without training. Qwen's math accuracy rose from 7.9 to 48.1 percent after changing 0.016 percent of its weights.

items.title: Nothing will release a screenless AI device
items.text: CEO Carl Pei wrote that the first AI product ships in December. It has no new screen and could not have been an app.

items.title: AI agents ordered four Uber rides in a week
items.text: During Halloween week, agents placed 4 rides and 500 food orders out of about 320 million. The CEO calls interest very early and limited.

items.title: Google will turn Gemini off in school accounts by default
items.text: Gemini and AI search for students stay off until the school turns them on. Each service is enabled separately, and the new controls arrive early next year.

items.title: Oppo is preparing a phone with a roughly 12,000 mAh battery
items.text: The device received MIIT certification, and the data lists an 11,460 mAh battery. This is a rumor: name and timing are unknown.

takeaway: Several stories today are about access: hosting logins, Google sign-in and data on a computer with a game launcher. Recommendation: check where your site and bot access keys are stored and which sessions your accounts have open.
